messages.content: "85 :     public static String escapeJava(String str) {\n86 :         return escapeJavaStyleString(str, false);\n87 :     }"

The failing test `testEscapeJavaWithSlash` is testing the `escapeJava` method in `StringEscapeUtils` class from Apache Commons Lang 2.4. The test expects that when the input string contains a slash (`/`), the output should be the same as the input because slashes are not valid characters to escape in a Java string.

However, based on the current bug report, it seems that in Commons Lang 2.4, the `escapeJava` method now escapes the slash character, which is not the expected behavior according to the test. Looking at the code snippet of the `escapeJava` method, it simply calls `escapeJavaStyleString` with `false` as the second argument.

This change to escape the slash character may have been introduced unintentionally as a side effect of a fix or modification in version 2.4 of Apache Commons Lang.

To fix this issue, the `escapeJava` method in the `StringEscapeUtils` class needs to be modified to exclude escaping the slash character when it is encountered in the input string.

Next, I will suggest the best locations to fix this issue.
The best locations to fix this issue would be:
```
org.apache.commons.lang.StringEscapeUtils.escapeJava(java.lang.String)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
